marks.gloss_en: after Ravin's report of Rav Asi's לא שנו אלא לחולה המרגיל -- איצטמיד חצביה דרב נחמן
they taught [nine kav] only for a sick man whose emission came by intercourse
נהי דתקן עזרא טבילה, נתינה מי תקן?! והאמר מר עזרא תיקן טבילה לבעלי קריין -- Ezra enacted immersion, not pouring (the cited dictum; no ObjectionKind for והאמר מר, kind svara)
Ezra enacted immersion for those who have had an emission
since all these amoraim and tannaim disagree about Ezra's [enactment] -- let us see what Ezra enacted
Ezra enacted forty se'a for a healthy man whose emission came by intercourse
one who was standing in prayer and water ran on his knees stops until the water ceases, and resumes praying
entertained: their dispute turns on one who delayed long enough to finish the whole prayer
one who was standing in prayer and remembered that he is a baal keri does not stop, but abridges
one who went down to immerse: if he can come up, cover himself and read before sunrise, he comes up, covers himself and reads
זבח רשעים תועבה -- אלא אמר רבא: הואיל וחטא... תפלתו תועבה
מתקיף לה רבא: והא זבח רשעים תועבה! -- an offering brought in sin is an abomination, so how can his prayer be a prayer?
Rabba: one who was praying and found feces in his place -- though he sinned, his prayer is a prayer
והתניא לצדדין -- another baraita has him move to the sides, not forward
לא קשיא: הא דאפשר, הא דלא אפשר -- forward where he can, to the sides where he cannot (= p_okimta_efshar, p_okimta_lo_efshar)
one standing in prayer who saw feces facing him walks forward until he has thrown it four cubits behind him
one who was standing in prayer and remembered he is a baal keri does not stop, but abridges
בשלמא למאן דאמר אפילו בכלים, היינו דקתני מכל מקום; אלא למאן דאמר בקרקע אין בכלים לא -- מכל מקום לאתויי מאי?
for the even-vessels view, R' Yehuda's 'in any case' is [what includes] vessels
לאתויי מים שאובין -- 'in any case' includes drawn water (= p_mikol_makom_sheuvin, held aliba the ground-only view)
for the ground-only view, 'in any case' comes to include drawn water
תנינא: במה דברים אמורים -- לעצמו, אבל לאחרים -- ארבעים סאה -- nine kav do not qualify one [to bless] for others
Rav Pappa: give me [the cup] to bless, for nine kav fell on me
a baal keri on whom nine kav of water were poured is pure -- that is said of [purity] for himself
the clause 'but for others forty se'ah' was taught only of a sick man whose emission was normal (hamargil)
R' Yehuda's 'forty se'ah in any case' was taught only of [water in] the ground, but in vessels -- no
Rav Chama would immerse on the eve of Passover in order to discharge the many their obligation
